Thanks for the demo last week — BlueBridge's legal and security teams asked for a concise proposal on how Redwood prices combined CCPA (data subject requests + opt-out tooling) and HIPAA (audit logs, HSM/KMS, residency) when purchased as a single compliance bundle. Our procurement lead would like to see a proposed term sheet showing:

- Line-item pricing for audit log retention tiers (1y / 3y / 7y)
- HSM seat vs usage-based KMS calls (examples for our 200k monthly API calls)
- Data residency add-on options across regions (US-east / US-west / EU)

Can you send a short term sheet and a recommended packaging approach? We prefer a single predictable OPEX number but need visibility into what can be one-time vs recurring.

Anna — thanks, and appreciated the clear ask. Attached is a first-pass term sheet and a pricing workbook (see attachments). High level notes in-line below and some suggested next steps.

Quick summary (ballpark for planning):
- Audit logs: $0.02 / GB-month for 1y retention, $0.017 / GB-month for 3y, $0.013 / GB-month for 7y. Long-retention tiers get a 15% volume discount at >10TB.
- KMS/HSM: two options — (A) HSM seat: $X,000 / month per HSM cluster (recommended for PHI-heavy workflows with FIPS/HSM requirement) or (B) managed KMS calls: $0.00003 / call (we can model your 200k calls -> ~$6/month) plus a small key-management admin fee.
- Data residency: regional residency add-on is a % surcharge on hosted usage (US-west/US-east 8% / EU 12%). Dedicated/private deployments are priced separately and can be in the term sheet as an appendix.
- Bundling discount: when CCPA+HIPAA items are contracted together with a 12-month or greater commit, we can offer an implementation credit that amortizes up to 50% of the onboarding SOW across the first 6 months of recurring billing.

Suggested packaging approach:
1) Base hosted API pricing for tokens/embeddings (kept separate)
2) Compliance bundle SKU that combines 1y audit log retention + managed KMS + US residency surcharge with option to upgrade retention or switch to HSM seats.
3) Provide a conservative default estimate for audit log storage based on your current volume (we used 3.1TB/month as an example in the workbook).

Next steps:
- I attached BBH-TermSheet-v1.pdf and the workbook. If helpful, Ben can run a short model that shows blended monthly OPEX under 12/24/36 month commitments.

Adding a couple pricing mechanics and a concession pathway that typically helps procurement move faster:

- Implementation credit structure: instead of a straight 50% amortization, offer a split: 30% upfront SOW credit + up to 40% back as usage credits over first 3 months if commit >= 12 months. This reduces initial cash flow impact while keeping a measurable OPEX discount.
- HSM seat concession: for enterprise pilots we sometimes offer first HSM cluster waived for 90 days (one-time) if customer signs a 12-month committed Dedicated or Private addendum.
- Audit log retention swap: allow a one-time free conversion (e.g., move from 1y -> 3y) within first 60 days of go-live to account for initial ingestion mis-estimates.

I'm happy to spin the numbers in the workbook to show invoice-level examples (monthly charge lines that map to their accounting).

-Ben

Looping in a short note from legal/finance perspective:

- If BlueBridge prefers a single OPEX line, we can provide a packaged monthly invoice with a labeled compliance add-on SKU. Finance will need the breakdown in the workbook for audit — we'll keep that internal but the invoice will show the bundle price.
- Term length sensitivity: smaller customers often ask for a 6-month pilot price; we should allow a higher effective unit price for pilots to protect amortization of onboarding. Suggest model: pilot = +18% on bundle list price for <=6 months.
- Billing cadence: we recommend monthly billing for audit log storage, KMS calls, and residency surcharges. HSM seat licenses are billed monthly but can be annually prepaid if they prefer.
